## Authentication

Every route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is an RS256 access token issued by Kobana's Authorization Server (Kobana Account) for the `kadu` resource. Kadu only verifies the token, using the public keys the AS publishes; it does not issue tokens. The organization is the `org` claim.

## Scopes

Scopes are required on every route, except `GET /v1/me`. Each request requires a single access level, and one level never substitutes for another:

| Level | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | read (`GET`) |
| `write` | create and update (`POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`) — and read |
| `delete` | removal (`DELETE`) |
| `import` | bulk import (no endpoint today) |
| `export` | bulk export (no endpoint today) |
| `all` | all of the levels above |

A token with `kadu/{resource}` scopes (e.g. `kadu/tasks`) is restricted to those resources, and the level applies only within them; `kadu/all` reaches every resource. A route's resource is the first segment after `/v1` (`/executions/{id}/logs` → `executions`). Resources: `activities`, `environments`, `executions`, `files`, `memberships`, `memories`, `organizations`, `repository`, `roles`, `schedules`, `secrets`, `system_events`, `tasks`, `todos`, `usage`, `users`, `webhook_deliveries`, `webhooks`, `workspaces`.

## User permissions

Besides scopes, a token issued for a person (with `email`) is limited to their role in the organization (`Role.permissions`): each route requires `agent.<resource>.<action>` (`list`, `read`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, and the actions `executions.run`, `webhook_deliveries.replay` and `repository.sync`), with the wildcards `*`, `agent.*` and `agent.<resource>.*`. A role that does not grant it responds `403 USER_PERMISSION_DENIED` (`details.required`); a person with no membership in the organization gets `403 NOT_A_MEMBER`. An integration token, with no person, is governed by scopes only. `GET /v1/me` does not check the role.

## Organization permissions

The routes for run, logs, webhooks, deliveries, environments, secrets, schedules, Task endpoint, repository and usage also respect the permissions Kobana grants the organization for the console screens. An operation that is not enabled responds `403 FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED`, with `details.permission`.

A token with no scope that Kadu recognizes reaches nothing beyond `/me`. Insufficient scope responds `403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, with `details.required` (the levels that would suffice).

## Contract

- Wire in `snake_case`; free-form maps (`custom_metadata`, `payload`, `parameters`…) are opaque.
- Monetary and cost values are `number` (USD in `*_usd`, reais in `*_brl`).
- Success: `{ data }` or `{ data, meta }`; error: `{ error: { code, message, details? } }` with `code` in UPPER_SNAKE.
- Cursor-based listings: `cursor` + `limit` (max. 100), ordering by `sort_by` + `sort_order`; `meta: { next_cursor, limit }`.
- `X-Idempotency-Key` on every `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` (24h per organization).
- `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` body up to 1 MiB; above that, `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`.
